abstract:
This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of combining low-dose radiotherapy to the intestines with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in patients with liver metastases from solid tumors.

Liver metastases often create an "immune desert" that makes immunotherapy less effective. Recent research has shown that low-dose irradiation of the gut (1 Gy) can reshape the gut microbiome and activate the immune system, potentially reversing resistance to immunotherapy.

This is a prospective, single-arm, single-center cohort study. We plan to enroll 120 patients with liver metastases from non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), colorectal cancer, or pancreatic cancer. All participants will receive a single low dose of radiotherapy to the intestine (1 Gy), followed by standard immune checkpoint inhibitors and chemotherapy.

The main goal of this study is to see how well the liver metastases respond to this combined treatment. We will also monitor survival, side effects, and changes in the gut bacteria and blood immune markers to understand how this treatment works. This strategy may provide a low-cost, low-toxicity new option for patients whose liver metastases have stopped responding to standard immunotherapy.

Background: Liver metastasis is a common cause of death in advanced solid tumors and is associated with systemic immune suppression, leading to primary resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Preclinical and clinical evidence suggests that low-dose irradiation of the gut (ILDR, 1-3 Gy) can induce the migration of regulatory dendritic cells (mregDCs) from mesenteric lymph nodes to tumor-draining lymph nodes, cross-activate CD8+ T cells, and reprogram metabolism, thereby synergizing with ICIs. The Chen et al. (Cancer Cell 2025) study demonstrated that ILDR (1-3 Gy) significantly improved overall survival in patients receiving SABR plus anti-PD-L1, with an inverted U-shaped dose-response relationship. This study aims to prospectively evaluate the efficacy and safety of ILDR combined with ICIs in patients with liver metastases from solid tumors.

Study Design: This is a prospective, single-arm, single-center, exploratory cohort study. A one-sided exact binomial test will be used to compare the liver metastasis ORR with historical controls. The study plans to enroll 120 patients in three cohorts: Cohort A (NSCLC, driver gene negative, after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy plus PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor progression, expected ORR 30% vs 10%), Cohort B (NSCLC, driver gene positive, after first-line targeted therapy progression, expected ORR 55% vs 35%), and Cohort C (colorectal/pancreatic cancer, after up to two lines of therapy progression, expected ORR 35% vs 15%). A two-stage execution rule with futility analysis will be applied.

Intervention: Patients will receive ILDR (1 Gy/1 fraction, IMRT/VMAT) targeting the jejunum, ileum, and mesentery (Dmean = 1 Gy) on Day 1. ICIs (PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors) will be administered 24-72 hours after ILDR, every 3 weeks, for up to 2 years. Combined chemotherapy regimens include docetaxel for Cohort A, platinum-based doublet for Cohort B, and XELOX/FOLFOX/FOLFIRI/AG for Cohort C.

Endpoints: The primary endpoint is liver metastasis objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1. Secondary endpoints include overall ORR, disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), safety (CTCAE 5.0), and multi-omics analysis (gut microbiome, metabolomics, immune profiling) of peripheral blood and stool samples.

Statistical Analysis: The primary endpoint will be analyzed using the Clopper-Pearson exact method for 95% CI. PFS and OS will be estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Multi-omics data will be analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Mann-Whitney U test, LEfSe, PLS-DA, and Spearman correlation analysis.
key_points_ko: 목표 환자 수는 총 120명이며, 췌장암 및 대장암 코호트(코호트 C)는 최대 2차 치료까지 진행한 환자가 대상입니다.
중재 치료로 장에 1 Gy의 저선량 방사선 치료(ILDR)를 1회 시행하고, 24~72시간 내에 면역관문억제제와 병용 항암화학요법을 시작합니다.
1차 평가지표는 RECIST v1.1에 따른 간전이 객관적 반응률(ORR)입니다.
초록에 생존기간이나 구체적인 수치 결과는 아직 제시되지 않았으며, 향후 역사적 대조군과 비교될 예정입니다.
summary_ko: 이 연구는 고형암 간전이가 있는 환자를 대상으로 장 저선량 방사선 치료(ILDR)와 면역관문억제제(ICI) 및 항암화학요법의 병용 치료 효과와 안전성을 평가합니다. 간전이는 면역치료에 저항성을 가지기 쉬우며, 장에 1 Gy의 저선량 방사선을 조사하여 장내 미생물을 재조형하고 면역 체계를 활성화하는 원리를 이용합니다. 췌장암을 포함한 120명의 환자가 참여하며, RECIST v1.1 기준 간전이 객관적 반응률(ORR) 등을 평가합니다.
title: Intestinal Low-Dose Radiotherapy Combined With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Solid Tumors With Liver Metastases
title_ko: 고형암 간전이 환자에서 장 저선량 방사선 치료와 면역관문억제제 병용 임상시험

trial.eligibility_ko:
선정 기준:
- 만 18세 이상 성인.
- ECOG 수행능력 상태 0~2.
- 예상 생존기간 3개월 이상.
- 조직학적 또는 세포학적으로 확진된 진행성 고형암 (코호트 C의 경우 최대 2차 치료까지 진행한 진행성 대장암 또는 췌장암).
- 방사선 또는 2가지 영상 검사로 확진된 간전이.
- RECIST v1.1 기준 간 내 측정 가능한 표적 병변 1개 이상.
- 방사선학적으로 안정된 뇌전이는 허용됨.

제외 기준:
- 방사선 치료 및 면역관문억제제 치료에 대한 금기증.
- 이전 면역관문억제제 치료 후 허용할 수 없는 독성 이력.
- 등록 전 6개월 이내 복부골반 방사선 치료 이력.
- CTCAE 5.0 기준 1등급 이하로 회복되지 않은 이전 항암 치료 부작용.
- 조절되지 않는 활성 전신 감염.
- 등록 전 2주 이내 항생제, 항진균제, 항바이러스제, 구충제 사용.
- 최대 직경이 4cm를 초과하는 병변 부하.
trial.eligibility_text:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥ 18 years, male or female.
* ECOG performance status 0-2.
* Expected survival ≥ 3 months.
* Histologically or cytologically confirmed advanced solid malignancies:

  * Cohort A: Advanced NSCLC with negative driver genes (EGFR/ALK/ROS1), disease progression during first-line platinum-based doublet chemotherapy combined with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors.
  * Cohort B: Advanced NSCLC with positive driver genes (EGFR/ALK/ROS1), disease progression during first-line targeted therapy.
  * Cohort C: Advanced colorectal or pancreatic cancer, disease progression during no more than two lines of therapy.
* Confirmed liver metastasis (pathologically or by 2 imaging modalities).
* At least 1 measurable intrahepatic target lesion per RECIST v1.1.
* Brain metastases are permitted if radiologically stable.
* Adequate major organ function within 7 days prior to enrollment:

  * Hematology: Absolute neutrophil count ≥ 1.5 × 10\^9/L, Platelets ≥ 100 × 10\^9/L, Hemoglobin ≥ 90 g/L.
  * Liver: Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 × ULN (≤ 3 × ULN for Gilbert's syndrome or liver metastasis); AST/ALT ≤ 2.5 × ULN (≤ 5 × ULN for liver metastasis).
  * Kidney: Serum creatinine ≤ 1.5 × ULN, or creatinine clearance ≥ 50 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault formula).

Exclusion Criteria:

* Contraindications to radiotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
* Prior unacceptable toxicity following immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
* History of abdominopelvic radiotherapy within 6 months prior to enrollment.
* Prior anti-tumor adverse events not recovered to CTCAE 5.0 Grade ≤ 1.
* Active uncontrolled systemic bacterial, viral, or fungal infection.
* Use of antibiotics, antifungals, antivirals, or antiparasitics within 2 weeks prior to enrollment.
* Any lesion burden with a maximum diameter \> 4 cm.
* Other standard exclusion criteria (e.g., pregnancy, lactation, severe comorbidities, etc.).
